implications.text: Opus 5 leads on both Artificial Analysis boards — one evaluator: AA Index 60.69 vs Fable 59.86 and Sol 58.89 (a 0.83-pt gap at the top), and GDPval-AA 1857.8 vs Fable 1746.06 (a 111.74-Elo margin). The independent aggregators do not confirm the order: Epoch's composite puts Sol first at 161.69 with Fable 161.55 above Opus 161.05, and Fable is #1 on LiveBench (83.4) and the Vals composite (75.1). The lead claim is scoped to the AA evaluator; the cross-board split is logged as an open question.
implications.falsifier: the AA order flips (any tracked model above 60.69 on the AA Index), or the non-AA aggregators (Epoch, LiveBench, Vals) converge on the AA order — the first kills the lead, the second kills the dissent

implications.text: OPEN — is the AA order the outlier? Arena style-control has Fable 5 #1 at 1507.6 with Opus 5 (max variant) at 1494.6, and the non-AA boards lean the same way: Fable tops LiveBench (83.4 vs Opus 80.5) and the Vals composite (75.1 vs 74.8), while Epoch puts Sol first with Fable above Opus. Reading 1: a real split — the AA evaluator's judged boards favor Opus while preference and mixed ground-truth boards favor Fable. Reading 2: settling noise — Arena private-variant testing is active, 13 Elo is within churn for a fresh board, and the Vals gap is 0.3. Reading 3: the AA order is an evaluator effect, not a field consensus. The evidence supports all three.
implications.falsifier: closes toward reading 1 or 3 if the next two publishes of Arena, LiveBench and Vals hold Fable ahead while AA holds Opus ahead; toward reading 2 if Opus overtakes on two of the three non-AA boards as variants settle

implications.text: Price-performance frontier, computed on AA index (higher is better) against cost per task (lower is better): Opus 5 ($2.34 / 60.69), Sol ($1.86 / 58.89), Kimi K3 ($0.86 / 57.11) and DS V4 Pro ($0.05 / 44.27) are Pareto-efficient. Fable 5 ($3.15 / 59.86) is the only tracked model strictly dominated — by its own stablemate, which scores higher and costs less. Caveat: all five cost inputs moved against the seed with the driver unresolved; frontier composition is provisional until it resolves.
implications.falsifier: driver resolution or the next AA refresh moves Fable's cost to $2.34 or below, lifts its index above 60.69, or drops any efficient point behind another

implications.text: DeepSeek's value position is an outlier, not a frontier-quality substitute: 885.4 index-points per task-dollar is 13x Kimi's 66.4 and 28-47x the three Western flagships (Sol 31.7, Opus 25.9, Fable 19.0). But it buys 44-level intelligence with the field's worst knowledge profile — Omniscience -10.02 (more wrong answers than right) at a 0.940 hallucination rate, highest of the five. Cheap capability, not cheap reliability.
implications.falsifier: DS cost-per-task revises up by roughly an order of magnitude on driver resolution, or its Omniscience index turns positive on the next AA refresh

implications.text: OPEN — what do the routing shares measure? The facts: DeepSeek moved 17.4% of OpenRouter tokens in the last complete week (displaced from #1 by newcomer xiaomi at 19.1%, with the partial current week back at 20.9%), Anthropic routed 9.1% of tokens but roughly 44% of code-category spend, OpenAI 6.9%. Reading 1: two demand lanes — DeepSeek moves volume, Anthropic monetizes code. Reading 2: a price artifact — token share overweights cheap tokens ($0.05 per task) exactly as spend share overweights the field's priciest models ($2.34–$3.15 per task), so neither is a customer count and both lanes may be bookkeeping. All figures are provider-level with a flagged unit ambiguity; none of this attributes demand to any single model.
implications.falsifier: closes toward reading 1 if the completed 07-27 week restores DeepSeek past xiaomi while Anthropic code-spend holds above ~35%; toward reading 2 if a spend-denominated share view reorders the token-share lanes

implications.text: Sol is the integrity story of this cycle: three open items — SWE-bench Verified withheld after METR's evaluation, a vendor-modified harness claim of 38.3 (custom settings, no declared tier) on the public puzzle set against an official Max-tier 7.78, and METR's cheating flag (a detected cheating rate higher than any public model they have evaluated). Every headline Sol number on this page needs the footnote before the comparison.
implications.falsifier: item-by-item: publication of the withheld benchmark with methodology, an official-harness verification of the 38.3, or a METR re-evaluation without the cheating flag each closes its item; all three closed empties the read

implications.text: OPEN — is the ARC-AGI-3 gap capability or coverage? Opus 5's 30.16 (High tier, the board record) stands against Sol's official 7.78 (Max tier) — but the record run cost $20,657 above the published per-run cap (waived), the vendor disputes the Sol figure with a modified-harness claim the board excludes, Fable has no verified score at any tier (the seed's 16.6 was withdrawn as unverifiable), and Kimi and DS were never evaluated. Reading 1: Opus holds genuine novelty headroom. Reading 2: a two-point board with non-comparable effort economics cannot rank the field. Both hold.
